title: Overfed: too much food at once
about: More food than the worms can eat does not wait for them: it composts. The core heats up, the air in the box is used up, and it starts to smell. Here somebody tips a whole bucket in, the sensors show it, the keeper stops further feeding, and you put it right.

steps.title: Speed the clock up
steps.why: Composting takes hours. Here 10 simulated minutes pass every second.

steps.title: Somebody tips a bucket in
steps.why: 4 kg of scraps straight into the box, past the hopper and the robot: about ten days' food for these worms. The load cells see the jump at once (the Worm box panel shows the weight).

expect.say: uneaten food in the box (simulation only): {v} g

steps.title: The box heats up and runs out of air
steps.why: Two signs, from two sensors. The core probe climbs away from the edge probe: the pile is composting. The gas sensor rises: the box is going airless. Each is enough for the keeper to hold feeding.

steps.title: You: take the excess out, add dry bedding
steps.why: Take out what is not yet eaten (3.5 kg) and mix in 800 g of dry shredded paper or cardboard. The bedding takes up moisture and lets air back in.

expect.say: uneaten food in the box (simulation only): {v} g

steps.title: The box settles
steps.why: The core cools back towards the edge and the smell goes. The keeper lets feeding go again on its own, with some margin so it does not flicker.
